rows.description: A teenager repeats a claim as true because it feels familiar, not remembering that it came from a forwarded message. Repetition increases belief.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student remembers a good idea and believes it was his own, when it came from a book or friend. Unintentional plagiarism can result from lost sources.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A careful worker notes sources while reading and asks how she knows a claim, separating what she saw, was told and inferred.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child recalls exactly where he was on a big day such as a family loss or a cricket win, and feels the picture is perfectly clear and true.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager vividly remembers where he was during a national event or a shock and is very sure, though details drift over time as with any memory.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Two friends recall a dramatic event differently and each is sure. They learn that emotional intensity increases confidence more than accuracy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A thoughtful adult accepts that vivid memories are meaningful and still checks details against records, and does not use them as unquestioned proof in disputes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child who learns a poem all in one evening forgets it in days. Learning packed into one session vanishes faster than learning spread out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who crams before tests remembers enough to pass but loses it soon after. Short repeated sessions build stronger and longer memory.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student spreads study across days, recalls answers without looking, and revisits material just as it begins to fade. It feels harder and works better.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
